title.zh: 分子氢分子氢弹性动量转移截面

summary: H2-on-H2 elastic momentum-transfer cross section in m^2 as a function of collision energy in eV: a single five-coefficient logarithmic polynomial on the clipped [0.03, 1.01e4] eV domain. The selector validation is kept: viscosity=True selects the documented same-fit fallback, and the selector must be a scalar boolean or integer. Negative energies are rejected.

capability: H2-on-H2 elastic momentum-transfer cross section in m^2 from collision energy in eV.
operation: Evaluate the H2-on-H2 elastic momentum-transfer cross section
collision energies and fallback selector -> cross section per energy
discovery.model: Single declared five-coefficient logarithmic-polynomial fit with a documented no-op fallback selector; no external-data interpolation and no rate integration.
discovery.geometry: None; scalar material function of collision energy with no spatial axis (coordinate: collision energy in eV; output in m^2).
discovery.boundary: Energies must be finite and nonnegative; values outside the [0.03, 1.01e4] eV fit range clip to the endpoints; the selector must be a scalar boolean or integer.

identity.relation: the H2-on-H2 elastic momentum-transfer cross section as a function of collision energy
identity.direction: collision energies and fallback selector -> cross section per energy
identity.definition: Energies are clipped to [0.03, 1.01e4] eV and the cross section is exp(polyval(log(E_clipped), a)) * 1e-4 m^2 with the five coefficients. viscosity=True selects the documented fallback, which evaluates the same momentum-transfer fit. Endpoint values repeat outside the clipped range.
identity.model: a single declared cross-section fit with a documented no-op fallback selector; no interpolation of external data and no rate integration
identity.geometry: none; a scalar material function of collision energy
identity.coordinates: collision energy in eV; output cross section in m^2
identity.boundary: energies must be finite and nonnegative; in-domain values outside the fit range clip to the range endpoints; the selector must be a scalar boolean or integer
assumptions: The coefficients and the fallback-selector convention are kept bit for bit; the fallback path emits no warning.
No external physical cross-section reference is bound; this residual stays open.

inputs.name: energy_ev
inputs.description: Collision energies at which the cross section is evaluated.
inputs.constraints: Finite and nonnegative. Values above or below the fit range are clipped to the range endpoints.

inputs.name: viscosity
inputs.description: Fallback selector: True selects the documented fallback, which evaluates the same momentum-transfer fit.
inputs.constraints: A scalar boolean or integer; arrays and non-integral scalars are rejected.

outputs.name: cross_section_m2
outputs.description: Elastic momentum-transfer cross section, one value per energy.
outputs.constraints: Finite and strictly positive for every accepted input.

preconditions: The caller accepts the clipping convention and the no-op fallback selector semantics.
supported: H2-on-H2 elastic momentum-transfer cross sections on the fit within (or clamped to) its declared energy range.
Scalar and array evaluation of any shape, including zero-dimensional inputs.
Rejecting negative energies and invalid selectors.
excluded: Maxwellian averaging of this cross section: use scirel.collisions.maxwellian-relative-speed-rate-average, which accepts this callable as its cross_section_m2 port.
Charge-exchange or ionization channels: different relations, provided by sibling assets.
Elastic cross sections for other species pairs: separate assets, not variants of this relation.
A cross-section model validated against an external atomic-physics reference; none is bound.

failure_semantics.invalid_input: Raises ValueError naming energy_ev for non-real, non-finite or negative energy inputs, or naming viscosity when that selector is not a scalar boolean/integer.
failure_semantics.runtime_failure: Not reachable on the declared domain: the fit is evaluated only on its clipped positive range. No iteration, no state and no partial results.

example.description: Evaluate the fit, confirm the same-fit fallback and selector validation, and confirm the negative-energy rejection.
example.expected: Finite strictly positive cross sections in m^2; the viscosity fallback reproducing the momentum-transfer values exactly; ValueError naming the scalar-boolean requirement for an array selector and naming nonnegativity for a negative energy.

scope: That the fit equals an independent evaluation of the coefficient set on the clipped domain to a relative tolerance of 1e-15.
The declared fallback: viscosity=True reproduces the momentum-transfer values exactly, and the scalar boolean/integer validation rejects arrays and non-integral scalars.
The endpoint clipping: values below and above the fit range repeat the endpoint values exactly.
The input contract: non-finite and negative energies are rejected with messages naming the quantity; a negative energy raises rather than being silently clipped.

Bit-exact agreement with an independent implementation of the same fit expressions on one- and two-dimensional grids, including the fallback path, together with the rejection witness; the comparison runs only when an external implementation root is configured.
verification.evidence_ceiling: An independent evaluation of the fit expressions covers every branch, clipping boundary and SI conversion; a NumPy-only installation passed scalar independent evaluation across 56 energies per branch, and all 62 fit/input tests passed with their original assertions and tolerances. This qualifies the stated empirical expression, not new experimental accuracy. No external experimental cross-section validation is bound, and redistribution permission remains separate.
known_limitations: The integrated input check rejects complex, boolean and numeric-string energies before float conversion; no coercion is performed. Valid real-input fit arithmetic is unchanged.
Neither branch is validated against an external atomic-physics reference; no external validation gap is closed here.
The viscosity selector is a no-op fallback convention, not a second fit; callers cannot obtain a distinct viscosity cross section for this species pair from this asset.
Energies outside the fit range silently return the endpoint value; this is the declared clipping convention, not an error.
The negative-energy rejection is an explicit precondition of this contract: a negative energy raises ValueError rather than returning the clipped endpoint.
The optional cross-implementation comparison runs only in an environment that supplies an external implementation root; it is skipped otherwise and covers only the compared grids.
Public distribution licensing remains pending a human decision.
